A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with the same title and author. All 37 pages of each version, including figures, equations and Appendices A–J, support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 presents theoretical bounds, proofs and analytically constructed distribution examples. It reports no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: V2 remains theoretical. Its new dataset images and empirical statistics are attributed to prior studies, rather than an evaluation performed by this work.

M1.justification: The adversarial risk objectives and zero-threshold classifier are retained. New primal formulations and transport-map arguments are proof constructions, not changes to a proposed training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version performs training or evaluation on datasets. V2 discusses MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR10 through prior work; these mentions and illustrative images do not establish new evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. Discussions of earlier surrogate bounds remain theoretical research comparisons.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an original experimental evaluation protocol. Revised distributional assumptions and perturbation conditions concern mathematical guarantees and examples.

E4.justification: No original ablations, robustness tests or empirical supplementary analyses appear in either version. V2's lower-bound example is a mathematical argument, while its dataset-ambiguity discussion interprets previously published evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or empirical uncertainty estimation. Noise conditions are theoretical assumptions.

E6.justification: Neither version contains original experimental result entries. Changed risk-bound constants are formal theoretical results; newly quoted dataset statistics are attributed to other studies.

T1.justification: V2's linear theorem explicitly assumes consistency and replaces the prefactor (3+sqrt(5))/2 with 1. Its distribution-dependent bound changes factors 6 and z/6 to 4 and z/4. It adds lower-bound Example 4 and transport-map extensions in Theorems 10 and 12, supported by Section 6 and Appendix I. Appendix D receives a different proof, the integral estimate is sharpened, and Gaussian-example conditions are corrected.

C1.justification: The three headline contributions remain. V2 drops the abstract's separate emphasis on non-adversarial bounds, replaces the introduction's first-result claim with a broader supremum-risk framework claim, and narrows the conclusion's unresolved optimality question to the concave bound.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands applicability and limitations: it connects dataset ambiguity to mass at eta*=1/2, explains the role of additive residual terms, and discusses uncertain transport-map assumptions for real datasets and open multiclass extensions. Section 4.3 also interprets the linear bound as near-optimal, replacing v1's largely unresolved optimality discussion.

D1.justification: Neither version provides an experimental implementation, hyperparameters, hardware information or a code/data release. Expanded mathematical derivations do not add implementation or experimental reproducibility information.

R1.justification: V2 adds references on dataset ambiguity and robustness, including Northcutt, Bartoldson and Dai, and explicitly credits Staib and Jegelka for the observation underlying Lemma 1. It removes proper-loss references associated with the replaced Appendix D and the Liu approximation-error discussion. The central comparisons with Li and Telgarsky and Mao remain.

P1.justification: The introduction, background and proof exposition are extensively rewritten. V2 creates a separate surrogate-risk-bounds subsection, moves sample-complexity discussion into related work, organizes related work under thematic headings, and substantially restructures the proofs and appendices.

P2.justification: V2 adds a four-panel dataset-image Figure 2, retains the previous distribution plots as Figure 3, and expands Figure 1's caption. Journal-template headers and an OpenReview placeholder are added; the basic single-column layout and existing illustrations remain.

improvement.justification: V2 improves exposition and adds substantive extensions and optimality analysis. However, Equation (32) and Appendix F Equation (57) invoke Lemma 5 to bound the perturbation term alone, although that lemma bounds the full surrogate-excess integrand. V1 explicitly handled near-zero scores separately. This material proof gap affects the central sharpened guarantees, making the net quality change uncertain.
